title: Methodology

batches.text: Settlements a solver executed on Base in the window that filled at least one order. One auction can settle as several batches.

trades.text: Orders filled inside those batches. An order filled in parts counts once per fill.

volume.text: USD value of filled orders. Each trade counts at the lower of its sell and buy value, priced with the token prices CoW used in that auction and Chainlink’s ETH/USD rate at settlement. With only one side priced, that side counts; with neither, the trade adds nothing.

share.text: A solver’s portion of all batches, trades or volume in the window.

gas.text: Gas units used by a solver’s settlements divided by trades filled. Units of gas, not cost. “Lowest gas / trade” considers only solvers with at least {minBatches} batches per day of the window.

swaps.text: Interactions in a settlement other than token approvals and WETH unwraps. Per trade: a solver’s swaps divided by the trades it filled.

batchValue.text: Volume divided by batches. Trades per batch is trades divided by batches.

networkAverage.text: Gas per trade and DEX swaps per trade across all solvers, weighted by trades.

entered.text: Share of the window’s auctions in which the solver submitted at least one solution. Only auctions that ended in a settlement count. “Average solver” is the mean over the table’s solvers that entered at least one auction.

winRate.text: Share of the auctions a solver entered that it won, alone or with other winners.

leadingSince.text: First day of the current unbroken run in which the same solver alone ranked #1 by daily share.

sources.text: Settlement events, receipts and token symbols on Base, the settlement contract’s on-chain solver allow-list, CoW Protocol’s solver-competition API, CoW’s solver registry and Chainlink’s ETH/USD feed.

attribution.text: Settlements sent through CoW’s flash-loan router are credited to the solver that won the auction.

registry.text: Status and submission addresses as CoW’s solver registry lists them for Base, plus addresses it does not list as active that settle on Base and are on the settlement contract’s on-chain solver allow-list; those are shown as active (today one: Rizzolver’s 0x8f58…5cb7). A retired address is one the registry marks inactive.

freshness.text: Updated every {minutes, plural, one {minute} other {# minutes}}. The figures run to block {block}, produced {date} at {time} UTC.
freshness.noData: Updated every {minutes, plural, one {minute} other {# minutes}}.

windows.text: Rolling, ending at the newest block in the data. Longer windows add up daily windows; rates are averaged per auction.

coverage.text: Settlement history goes back {chain, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} and auction history {auction, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Volume, Entered and Win rate need auction data, so in a longer window they cover only the days that have it, and a note says so.
coverage.noData: Volume, Entered and Win rate need auction data, so in a longer window they cover only the days that have it, and a note says so.

names.text: From CoW’s public solver registry. Solvers without a public name are shown by address.

disclosure: Fiberscope is built by Fibrous, which also runs a solver on CoW Protocol. Every solver, Fibrous included, is measured by the same open-source code.
